title: Karnataka High Court Grants Actor Duniya Vijay Divorce, Orders Rs 2 Crore Alimony
excerpt: A division bench dissolved the actor's 27-year marriage on grounds of cruelty, overturning a Bengaluru family court ruling, and ordered a Rs 2 crore one-time settlement within two months.
body:
• A Karnataka High Court division bench of Justices D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan granted a divorce to Kannada actor Duniya Vijay and his wife Nagarathna on Thursday, September 3, on grounds of cruelty — overturning a Bengaluru family court order that had rejected his plea in June 2024.
  • The court directed Vijay to pay a one-time alimony of Rs 2 crore to Nagarathna within two months, failing which the amount would attract 6% annual interest. The bench weighed the wife's circumstances, the couple's three children, and the actor's financial standing in the film industry.
  • The couple married in 1999. Their dispute has been before the courts for 13 years: a first divorce petition filed in 2013 was withdrawn after a 2014 reconciliation, a fresh petition was filed in 2018, and the family court dismissed it for unproven cruelty claims.
  • The bench observed that fame offers no exception in matrimonial law, noting that the values public figures portray on screen should be reflected in their personal lives as well.

The Karnataka High Court on Thursday dissolved the 27-year marriage of Kannada film actor, director and producer Duniya Vijay and his wife Nagarathna, granting the actor a divorce on grounds of cruelty and ordering him to pay Rs 2 crore as one-time alimony.

The Order: Rs 2 Crore in Two Months

A division bench comprising Justices D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan passed the order after weighing Nagarathna's personal circumstances, the welfare of the couple's three children, and Vijay's financial standing and stature in the Kannada film industry, according to IANS. The Rs 2 crore settlement must be paid as a one-time amount within two months; if the actor defaults, the outstanding sum will accrue interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

https://x.com/XpressBengaluru/status/2097530257041686535

The order brings an end to a marital dispute that has played out in the courts for more than a decade, and drew wide attention in Karnataka's film circles, where Vijay is one of the industry's most recognisable faces.

"The good conduct and values portrayed by public figures on screen should be reflected in their personal lives as well."

— Karnataka High Court division bench, in the divorce order

A 13-Year Courtroom Saga

Vijay and Nagarathna married in 1999 and have three children. The dispute first reached the courts in 2013, when Vijay approached a Bengaluru family court seeking divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion, with issues over the care and upbringing of the children also surfacing during the proceedings.

The couple later attempted to resolve their differences. In 2014, reconciliation efforts followed and Vijay withdrew his first divorce petition after the two decided to resume their married life. But the differences resurfaced in the years that followed, and he filed a fresh petition in 2018, alleging among other grievances that Nagarathna had failed to properly care for his parents.

In June 2024, the family court rejected that petition, ruling that the cruelty charges had not been established and that the grounds cited by Vijay were not proven. Nagarathna had opposed the dissolution throughout, even as Vijay remained unwilling to resume cohabitation. On appeal, the High Court took into account the prolonged breakdown of the marriage and the welfare of the wife and children, and allowed the divorce.

Career and Personal Life in the Spotlight

Vijay, popularly known as "Duniya" Vijay after his breakthrough 2007 film Duniya, has built a career as an actor, director and producer in the Kannada film industry. His personal life has stayed in the headlines alongside it: sources close to the actor have said he has been living separately with his partner Keerthi Gowda. Meanwhile, his daughter Monisha Vijay Kumar is set to make her acting debut as a heroine in City Lights, a film directed by her father.

The case has been one of the longest-running personal controversies around the star, and the High Court's verdict marks its formal legal conclusion.

What Comes Next

The clock is now ticking on the Rs 2 crore payment, due within two months with interest running on default. The parties have the option of challenging the order before an appropriate forum, including the Supreme Court. News18 Kannada reported that the actor has also been entrusted with complete responsibility for the couple's three children.

Beyond the alimony figure, the verdict carries a message from the judiciary that celebrity status cuts no slack in family court — a remark that has already made the order one of the most discussed matrimonial rulings in Sandalwood in recent years.
